about: Galaxies as formulas, fitted to their photographs by tools/galaxy_fit.py (see there for what each number is). Lengths in kpc along the galaxy's own axes (axes: the long axis, the pole, the short axis, galactic); centrePc galactic, parsecs. photoMetadata: where the photograph has the galaxy.

photoMetadata.about: pixel (col, row) of a place (x, z) of the disc, kpc along its long and short axes: middlePx + (x longAxisPx + z cosTilt shortAxisPx) / kpcPerPx; the photograph's light there is how many stars there are

detail.about: rows along the long axis, columns along the short one; the natural log of the light over the formula, in sixteenths

faceMap.about: the face matrix: the disc from above, rows along its long axis, columns along its short one; colours as light^(1/2.2). The face-on picture as it is, turned onto the disc's axes by tools/galaxy_views.py

sideMap.about: the side matrix: for each of 'radii' radii from the middle out to radiusKpc, the light at 'heights' heights from -heightKpc to +heightKpc (0-255, each row's brightest 255), from the edge-on picture as drawn

lens.about: within radiusKpc the heights are pushed apart by up to 1 + strength in the middle (y + strength dome h tanh(y / h), dome = sqrt(1 - (R / radiusKpc)^2), h = (0.12 dome + 0.02) of the radius); extraLight of the stars in a flattened Gaussian of extraRadiusKpc
